Bill number: HB0522
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 386
 By Taylor

 HOUSE BILL 522

 By Reedy

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 16;
 Title 37 and Title 49, relative to student behavior.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 6, Part 3, is amended by

adding the following as a new section:

 (a) This section is known and may be cited as the "Early Behavioral Intervention

 and Reporting Act."

 (b) As used in this section, "early warning signs" means evidence of a student's

 safety, health, or behavioral issues and includes, but is not limited to, indicators of a

 student engaging in or being the victim of harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyber-

 bullying; making or receiving threats of violence; and exhibiting signs of substance

 abuse, mental health issues, self-harm, or suicidal ideation.

 (c) Each LEA and public charter school shall implement a computer-based

 system that teachers and school staff must use to input data of early warning signs

 demonstrated by students enrolled in the LEA or public charter school. Each LEA and

 public charter school shall ensure that each teacher and school staff member is trained

 to identify early warning signs and on how to input data into the computer-based system.

 (d) The computer-based system implemented pursuant to subsection (c) must:

 (1) Align with the requirements in § 49-6-4503; the School Discipline Act,

 compiled in part 41 of this chapter; and the school safety plans adopted by the

 LEA or public charter school pursuant to the Schools Against Violence in

 Education (SAVE) Act, compiled in part 8 of this chapter;

 (2) Include a database that is capable of receiving and maintaining

 student data entered by teachers and school staff on the early warning signs

 demonstrated by its students; and

 (3) Immediately notify the LEA's or public charter school's personnel

 serving on the LEA's or public charter school's threat assessment team created

 pursuant to § 49-6-2701 when an early warning sign is entered into the system

 for a student.

 (e) The LEA or public charter school personnel receiving a notification of an

 early warning sign of a student pursuant to subdivision (d)(3) shall review the

 notification, and any notifications of the student previously received, and determine

 whether further action is needed to address the student's behavior of an early warning

 sign.

 (f) Each LEA and public charter school shall annually submit a report to the

 department of education summarizing the data collected in the immediately preceding

 school year and the interventions provided, if any.

 (g) Reports made pursuant to this section must comply with the Family

 Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) (20 U.S.C. § 1232g); § 10-7-504; the Data

 Accessibility, Transparency, and Accountability Act, compiled in chapter 1, part 7 of this

 title; and all other relevant privacy laws.

 (h) If the commissioner of education finds that an LEA or public charter school is

 not complying with this section, then the commissioner may withhold state funds, in an

 amount determined by the commissioner, from the LEA or public charter school until the

 LEA or public charter school is in compliance with this section.

 SECTION 2. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2701, is amended by adding

"and public charter school" after "Each LEA", adding "or public charter school" after "LEA"

wherever it appears in the section, adding "or public charter school's" after "LEA's" in subsection

(b), adding "or public charter school governing body" after "local board of education" in

subsection (e), and adding "or the director of the public charter school" after "the director of

schools" in subsection (e).

 SECTION 3. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-2702(b), is amended by adding

"or public charter school" after "LEA" and adding "or public charter school's" after "LEA's".

 SECTION 4. This act takes effect July 1, 2025, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
The bill would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to use a computer-based system for teachers and staff to record students’ early warning signs of safety, health, or behavioral issues. These signs include bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health concerns, self-harm, and suicidal thoughts. Schools would have to train teachers and staff to recognize and enter the signs. The system would have to meet the bill’s cited discipline and school safety requirements, keep the entered data, and immediately notify personnel on the school’s threat assessment team when a sign is entered. Those personnel would review the new notice and any earlier notices for the student and decide whether further action is needed.

Each LEA and public charter school would have to report annually to the department of education on data collected during the previous school year and any interventions provided. Reports would have to comply with the cited privacy laws. If an LEA or public charter school did not comply, the commissioner of education could withhold an amount of state funding the commissioner determines until it complies. The bill would also add references to public charter schools and their officials in Tennessee Code Annotated, §§ 49-6-2701 and 49-6-2702(b). It would take effect July 1, 2025.
</summary>

assessments.summary_quote: These signs include bullying, threats of violence, substance abuse, mental health concerns, self-harm, and suicidal thoughts.
assessments.rationale: Captures several examples but omits harassment, intimidation, and cyber-bullying and does not convey that both perpetrators and victims, and both makers and recipients of threats, are included.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would require each local education agency (LEA) and public charter school to use a computer-based system for teachers and staff to record students’ early warning signs of safety, health, or behavioral issues.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the required system, covered educational entities, teacher and staff use, and student information to be recorded.

assessments.summary_quote: Schools would have to train teachers and staff to recognize and enter the signs.
assessments.rationale: In context, conveys the covered schools’ obligation to train teachers and staff in both identification and data entry.

assessments.summary_quote: The system would have to meet the bill’s cited discipline and school safety requirements
assessments.rationale: Conveys alignment generally, but does not identify the separate § 49-6-4503 requirements or the obligation to align with each entity’s adopted SAVE Act safety plans.

assessments.summary_quote: The system would have to meet the bill’s cited discipline and school safety requirements, keep the entered data
assessments.rationale: Together with the preceding description of teacher and staff data entry, conveys the system’s required data-receiving and retention functions.

assessments.summary_quote: immediately notify personnel on the school’s threat assessment team when a sign is entered.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the notification trigger, immediacy, and required threat assessment team recipients.

assessments.summary_quote: Those personnel would review the new notice and any earlier notices for the student and decide whether further action is needed.
assessments.rationale: Conveys review of both current and prior notifications and the determination whether further action is necessary.

assessments.summary_quote: Each LEA and public charter school would have to report annually to the department of education on data collected during the previous school year and any interventions provided.
assessments.rationale: Includes the reporting entities, recipient, annual frequency, reporting period, and required contents.

assessments.summary_quote: Reports would have to comply with the cited privacy laws.
assessments.rationale: Conveys privacy compliance generally but does not identify the specified protections or include the additional requirement to comply with all other relevant privacy laws.

assessments.summary_quote: If an LEA or public charter school did not comply, the commissioner of education could withhold an amount of state funding the commissioner determines until it complies.
assessments.rationale: Conveys the noncompliance condition, commissioner’s discretionary authority and control over the amount, and withholding until compliance.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would also add references to public charter schools and their officials in Tennessee Code Annotated, §§ 49-6-2701 and 49-6-2702(b).
assessments.rationale: Identifies the amendment target and general charter-school expansion, but does not convey the specific inclusion of charter governing bodies and directors in subsection (e) or the scope of the other insertions.

assessments.summary_quote: The bill would also add references to public charter schools and their officials in Tennessee Code Annotated, §§ 49-6-2701 and 49-6-2702(b).
assessments.rationale: Identifies § 49-6-2702(b) and conveys its expansion to public charter schools; the exact possessive and nonpossessive insertion wording is not independently material.
